symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of sequential recruitment decisions.

symbols.name: I
symbols.def: A nonempty subset of subgroup indices.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: A fixed bound on every local scenario coordinate.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: The finite cardinality of the declared scenario set.

symbols.name: \Delta_M
symbols.def: The simplex of probability weights on the declared scenarios.

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: \(x=(x_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}\) is a generic score state.

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: \(q=(q_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}\) is a generic information-clock state.

symbols.name: \mu
symbols.def: \(\mu=(\mu_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}\) denotes an arbitrary Gaussian mean vector.

symbols.name: \mathcal F_i
symbols.def: The sigma-field generated by recruitment randomization and observed subgroup-outcome pairs through time \(i\).

symbols.name: \pi_n
symbols.def: A randomized rule generating \(A_i\) from observed history.

symbols.name: \Pi_n
symbols.def: The predictable policy class constructed in Definition 1.

symbols.name: \mathcal F_t
symbols.def: The filtration generated by observed time-changed scores, allocation clocks, and exogenous randomization through time \(t\).

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: \(u(t)=(u_j(t))_{j\in\mathcal J}\) gives instantaneous subgroup allocation fractions.

symbols.name: \mathcal U
symbols.def: The observed-filtration relaxed-control class constructed in Definition 2.

symbols.name: W_j
symbols.def: Independent standard Brownian motions indexed by \(j\in\mathcal J\).

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A positive smoothing width for closed-test margins.

symbols.name: B_{n,\delta}^{\pm}(\lambda)
symbols.def: The infimum over finite policies of prior-weighted risk after replacing each miss indicator by \(f_\delta^{\pm}\).

symbols.name: B_\delta^{\pm}(\lambda)
symbols.def: The infimum over relaxed controls of prior-weighted risk after replacing each miss indicator by \(f_\delta^{\pm}\).

symbols.name: F_\lambda
symbols.def: The reference-law Bayes value with terminal datum \(\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_mZ_m\ell_m\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D=\{(t,x,q):0\leq t\leq1,\ x\in\mathbb R^K,\ q\in[0,1]^K,\ \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}q_j=t\}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak E
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak E=(K,M,H,(h^m)_{m=1}^M,w,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}})\), with every scalar other than the integer dimensions represented as a binary rational and with the membership and null-boundary-closure relations supplied as exact finite incidence data.

symbols.name: b_{\mathfrak E}
symbols.def: The total binary length of the rational and incidence encoding \(\mathfrak E\).

symbols.name: \underline V_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The dual lower endpoint returned from the finite encoding \(\mathfrak E\) at tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

symbols.name: \overline V_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The primal upper endpoint returned from the finite encoding \(\mathfrak E\) at tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

standard.name: Gaussian sequential experiment with known unit variance

assumptions.condition: Under scenario \(m\), \(\mu_j=h_j^m/\sqrt n\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\).
For every \(m\) and \(I\in\mathcal I\), the vector with coordinate \(h_j^m\mathbf 1\{j\notin I\}\) at each \(j\in\mathcal J\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_0\).

novel.justification: A confirmatory design can prespecify a finite collection of clinically relevant local alternatives and their coordinatewise null-boundary projections; this makes every intersection-null boundary an explicit stress scenario without restricting recruitment.

assumptions.condition: For each \(i\), the conditional law of \(A_i\) is \(\mathcal F_{i-1}\)-measurable and does not depend on the unknown scenario label.
The control \(u(t)\) is progressively measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_t\).

definitions.name: \Pi_n
definitions.construction: \(\Pi_n=\{\pi_n:\Pr_{\pi_n}(A_i\in\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{i-1})\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\text{ is }\mathcal F_{i-1}\text{-measurable for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal U
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal U=\{u:[0,1]\to\Delta(\mathcal J):u(t)\text{ is progressively measurable with respect to }\mathcal F_t\}\).

definitions.name: fixed arithmetic-mean closed e-test
definitions.construction: At horizon \(n\), set \(\delta_j^{\mathrm e}=1\), compute \(E_{j,n}=\exp(X_{j,n}-Q_{j,n}/2)\), compute \(E_{I,n}=|I|^{-1}\sum_{j\in I}E_{j,n}\) for every \(I\in\mathcal I\), and reject elementary null \(j\) exactly when \(a_{j,n}=\min_{I\ni j}(E_{I,n}-20)\geq0\).

definitions.name: continuous terminal-envelope risks
definitions.construction: Replace each factor \(\mathbf 1\{a_j(x,q)<0\}\) in \(\ell_m(x,q)\) by \(f_\delta^-(a_j(x,q))\) or \(f_\delta^+(a_j(x,q))\), evaluate at the finite or diffusion terminal state, and take the corresponding Bayes infimum to obtain \(B_{n,\delta}^{\pm}(\lambda)\) and \(B_\delta^{\pm}(\lambda)\).

definitions.name: generalized-terminal comparison handle
definitions.construction: Use half-relaxed limits of the continuous terminal envelopes on \(\mathcal D\), combine them with the virtual-score common-drift translation, and propagate statewise viability along zero-allocation faces for the operator \(\mathcal G_\lambda\).

definitions.name: finitely encoded certificate instance
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak E=(K,M,H,(h^m)_{m=1}^M,w,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}})\) is encoded by binary integers, binary rationals, and the exact finite lists defining \(\mathcal H_0\) and its null-boundary projections; validity checks consist of rational inequalities, normalization, positivity, and list membership.

definitions.name: explicit certificate resolution schedule
definitions.construction: From \(\mathfrak E\), compute \(r_\delta\), \(\delta_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(\eta_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(\Delta t_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(\Delta x_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(\Delta q_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(z_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(\Delta z_{\mathrm{cert}}\), \(r_{\lambda,\mathrm{cert}}\), and \(p_{\mathrm{cert}}\) by their displayed formulas; use the viable lattice with time spacing \(\Delta t_{\mathrm{cert}}\), allocation-clock spacing \(\Delta q_{\mathrm{cert}}\), score box \([-R_{\mathrm{cert}},R_{\mathrm{cert}}]^K\), score spacing \(\Delta x_{\mathrm{cert}}\), a standardized Gaussian box \([-z_{\mathrm{cert}},z_{\mathrm{cert}}]^K\) partitioned into cells of width at most \(\Delta z_{\mathrm{cert}}\), and an \(\ell_1\) prior net of radius at most \(r_{\lambda,\mathrm{cert}}\).

definitions.name: finite monotone primal-dual certificate algorithm
definitions.construction: For each prior-net point \(\lambda\), propagate \(F_\lambda\) with terminal datum \(\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_mZ_m\ell_m\) backward on the displayed resolution schedule over vertex allocations by order-preserving multilinear interval interpolation. Integrate each Gaussian transition by outward-rounded cell probabilities on the truncated standardized Gaussian box and assign the certified Gaussian tail mass adversarially to the lower and upper ranges. Enclose every scenario oracle by the same recursion at point-mass priors, maximize the lower Bayes-regret bound over the finite prior net, solve the finite scenario-risk linear program over the resulting Bayes policies, and return its primal policy mixture and dual prior together with the separated interval error ledger.

definitions.name: null-indexed one-sided inversion
definitions.construction: For each \(j\in\mathcal J\) and \(s\leq n\), invert \(\exp\{(S_{j,s}-\mu_j N_{j,s})/\sqrt n-N_{j,s}/(2n)\}\) at threshold \(1/\gamma_j\) to obtain \(B_{j,s}\).

statements.statement: Supporting corollary (Vovk--Wang arithmetic e-merging and the closed-testing principle): for every \(n\), every \(\pi_n\in\Pi_n\), and every \(\mu\in\mathbb R^K\), \(\mathbb P_\mu\{\mathcal R_n\cap\{j\in\mathcal J:\mu_j\leq0\}\neq\varnothing\}\leq\alpha=0.05\).
statements.justification: This cited corollary records the confirmatory guarantee held fixed while recruitment is optimized; it is not a novelty-bearing result.
statements.gap: Vovk and Wang establish arithmetic e-merging, and closed testing converts valid intersection tests into strong familywise error control; the displayed Gaussian specialization is a direct supporting corollary.
statements.consumer: It lets rpact-style enrichment workflows optimize enrollment without recalibrating the declared threshold.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\delta<1\), \(0<\eta\leq1\), prior \(\lambda\), and horizon \(n\), \(0\leq B_{n,\delta}^+(\lambda)-B_{n,\delta}^-(\lambda)\leq\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\eta)\) and \(0\leq B_\delta^+(\lambda)-B_\delta^-(\lambda)\leq\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\eta)\). The same inequalities hold for every oracle value, and \(\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\sqrt\delta)\to0\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\), without a positive lower bound on any allocation clock.
statements.justification: This modulus is the boundary-stability device that replaces false anti-concentration under adaptive freezing.
statements.gap: The diffusion comparators of Wager and Xu and Adusumilli use regular functionals; neither gives a uniform comparison across closed-test equality atoms.
statements.consumer: The explicit modulus is one component of an auditable error budget for a certified recruitment table.

statements.statement: The fixed Gaussian grid experiment is exactly embedded by vertex controls in the score diffusion, and the strict extension from the regular-payoff results of Wager and Xu and Adusumilli holds: arbitrary predictable policies, zero-allocation faces, and the discontinuous closed-test terminal loss satisfy \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|\to0\), \(c_{n,m}\to c_m\) for every \(m\), and \(V_n\to V\). Moreover, for each \(\epsilon>0\) there are predictable finite-horizon policies whose scenario-risk vectors converge coordinatewise to that of an \(\epsilon\)-optimal diffusion control.
statements.justification: It identifies the attainable local-power regret frontier for the fixed confirmatory test.
statements.gap: Adusumilli's 2026 theorem gives subsequential allocation-process representations and Adusumilli's 2025 convergence theorem uses Hölder data; this theorem adds a discontinuous closure payoff and legal boundary atoms.
statements.consumer: It converts a continuum recruitment solution into asymptotically valid finite-stage policies for interAdapt-style designs.

statements.statement: The minimax values obey \(V_n=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}\{\inf_{\pi_n\in\Pi_n}\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_mL_n(\pi_n,m)-\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_mc_{n,m}\}\) and \(V=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}\{\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_mL(u,m)-\sum_{m=1}^M\lambda_mc_m\}\), with attained least-favorable priors. For every \(\epsilon>0\), a finite mixture of Bayes best responses that are Markov in \((t,(X_j(t),Q_j(t))_{j\in\mathcal J},(b_m^\lambda)_{m=1}^M)\) is an \(\epsilon\)-saddle control and has every scenario regret at most \(V+\epsilon\).
statements.justification: The least-favorable prior converts robust enrichment into posterior-state control without mistaking one Bayes rule for a minimax policy.
statements.gap: Burnett and Jennison and Ballarini et al. take the prior as an input; they do not construct the adversarial prior or a simultaneous scenario-risk saddle mixture.
statements.consumer: It supplies the robust scenario weights and policy mixture needed to populate a confirmatory trial design specification.

statements.statement: For every valid finite binary-rational encoding \(\mathfrak E\), the finite monotone primal-dual certificate algorithm using the explicit resolution schedule terminates. It performs at most \(MKN_{\mathrm{prior}}N_{\mathrm{state}}N_{\mathrm{quad}}\) interval transition evaluations at \(p_{\mathrm{cert}}\)-bit fractional precision, followed by a finite linear program with at most \(N_{\mathrm{prior}}\) policy columns and \(M\) scenario rows, and returns \(\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}\) with \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}-\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\). Its eight-entry ledger separately bounds terminal regularization, score-box exit, Gaussian-tail truncation, Gaussian-cell quadrature, time-score-clock interpolation, prior-net discretization, oracle offsets, and outward rounding by \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}/8\) each. The algorithm returns an attained net prior and a finite mixture of net Bayes policies with maximum diffusion scenario regret at most \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}\); for all sufficiently large \(n\), boundary-stable policy transfer yields a predictable \(\pi_n\) with \(\max_m r_{n,m}(\pi_n)\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}+o(1)\).
statements.justification: The finite input model, resolution schedule, stopping bound, interval precision, and separated errors make the multidimensional certificate independently reproducible from primitive scenario data.
statements.gap: Baas, ter Schure, and van Rosmalen provide a scalar finite-horizon recursion, and Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu provide an approximate sparse enrichment program; those works inform the construction but do not certify this continuum minimax value or a response-adaptive policy mixture.
statements.consumer: The certificate can be attached to recruitment tables used by rpact and to finite-stage decision rules used by interAdapt.

statements.statement: Supporting corollary (Howard et al. and Ville inversion): for every predictable policy and every mean vector \(\mu=(\mu_j)_{j\in\mathcal J}\), \(\mathbb P_\mu\{\mu_j\geq B_{j,s}\text{ for all }j\in\mathcal J\text{ and }0\leq s\leq n\}\geq1-\alpha\). If \(N_{j,s}=0\), then \(B_{j,s}=-\infty\).
statements.justification: This cited Ville-inversion corollary supplies simultaneous reporting alongside the optimized design; it is not a novelty-bearing result.
statements.gap: Howard et al. provide time-uniform supermartingale inversion; subgroupwise allocation of error and a union bound give this direct supporting corollary, including the zero-information endpoint.
statements.consumer: Trial reports obtain simultaneous one-sided effect sequences even when the optimal policy stops sampling a subgroup.

statements.statement: In the special case \(K=2\), \(\mathcal H_0=\{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\}\), \(w_1=w_2=1/2\), and \(n=1\), symmetry yields \(V_1=\overline\Phi(\log 39-1/2)/4\).
statements.justification: The exact reduction checks normalization, closure, oracle subtraction, and least-favorable symmetry in the smallest nontrivial instance.
statements.gap: This is a sanity reduction rather than a novelty claim; it anchors the general frontier to an exactly solvable Gaussian case.
statements.consumer: It provides a unit test for any implementation of the finite Bellman recursion and certificate.

statements.statement: Can one prove comparison and uniqueness for bounded semicontinuous viscosity sub- and supersolutions of \(\mathcal G_\lambda F=0\) on \(\mathcal D\), with the generalized terminal traces selected by the fixed closed-test payoff, at every viable off-origin state including \(Q_j(t)=0\) faces and threshold-equality states?
statements.justification: A statewise uniqueness theorem would turn the initial-value envelope selection into a complete generalized-terminal HJB theory.
statements.gap: Adusumilli's comparison theorem covers Hölder data; the initial-state modulus here does not identify every off-origin boundary trace.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would justify reusable feedback values after arbitrary interim states, rather than only design-time evaluation from the origin.

sampling_model.design: A predictable randomized recruitment rule chooses one prespecified subgroup at each of \(n\) enrollment times; the design variable is the recruitment policy, while the arithmetic-mean closed e-test is fixed.
sampling_model.units: Independent standardized Gaussian responses arrive sequentially from the chosen subgroup under the local mean vector \(h^m/\sqrt n\).
sampling_model.treatment: The index \(A_i\) denotes subgroup recruitment rather than a randomized treatment label; each response represents a standardized treatment-control contrast with known unit variance.
sampling_model.overlap: No forced exploration is imposed: \(N_{j,n}=0\) and \(Q_j(1)=0\) are admissible.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no estimated nuisance functions in the core Gaussian experiment; unknown variance, delayed outcomes, and patient-level regression adjustment are outside scope.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives subsequential joint weak representations of score and allocation processes for arbitrary adaptive experiments.
Theorem 1 gives uniqueness for a Hölder-continuous viscosity solution and Section 3.2 derives discrete-to-PDE convergence under regular data.
Theorem 1 derives a weak-signal controlled diffusion for Lipschitz state-dependent sequential randomization.
Section 3 constructs finite-horizon design-optimal e-values by a scalar-state dynamic program for single-arm binary trials.
Sections 2 and 4 transform a discretized two-stage enrichment optimization into a sparse linear program and report approximately optimal designs.
The paper derives a Bayes-optimal enrichment rule for a specified prior while a fixed multiple-testing procedure controls strong FWER.
The paper optimizes subgroup selection and design parameters by prior-weighted utility under frequentist error control.
Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 establish the central role and admissibility of arithmetic e-value averaging.
Theorem 1 and the mixture method construct nonasymptotic time-uniform scalar confidence boundaries.
The paper develops posterior-state dynamic programming and a low-information diffusion approximation for a terminal action problem.

tldr: The novelty-bearing kernel fixes the arithmetic-mean closed e-test and characterizes how adaptive subgroup recruitment approaches a minimax local-power regret frontier despite discontinuous rejection surfaces, threshold atoms, and zero-allocation faces. A quantitative virtual-score envelope comparison supports diffusion value and policy transfer without forced exploration; finite-scenario duality then gives least-favorable priors and posterior-state controls. A finitely encoded, monotone primal-dual dynamic program uses an explicit tolerance-dependent mesh, Gaussian truncation and quadrature, prior net, termination bound, and separated interval ledger to certify the multidimensional frontier. Strong familywise error and simultaneous one-sided confidence sequences are cited supporting corollaries of arithmetic e-merging with closed testing and Howard--Ville inversion, respectively. Global generalized-terminal HJB uniqueness remains a first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Existing enrichment designs optimize a chosen-prior utility or a discretized two-stage program, and existing adaptive-experiment diffusions transfer regular risk functionals. They do not characterize minimax regret for the discontinuous rejection vector of a fixed closed e-test when legal recruitment creates threshold atoms and zero-information faces, nor do they provide a primitive-input numerical certificate for that multidimensional frontier.
project_justification.niche: Holding the confirmatory test and its established error guarantee fixed isolates the design question of which subgroup to recruit. The resulting local Gaussian score experiment combines a nonregular terminal decision with an auditable finite-scenario robust-control problem.
project_justification.fill: The project derives a quantitative boundary-stability modulus, proves convergence of values and risk vectors without forced exploration, reduces robust design to a least-favorable posterior-control problem, and specifies a terminating interval Bellman algorithm whose tolerance-dependent discretizations and error contributions certify an implementable policy mixture.

related_work: Adusumilli's 2025 Econometrica article provides the nearest Bayes and minimax diffusion-PDE architecture and numerical policy recovery; the frontier theorem targets its unresolved discontinuous-terminal and zero-allocation regime. Adusumilli's 2026 allocation-process representation supplies the broad finite-to-continuous experiment donor, while the quantitative closed-test envelope comparison supplies the missing risk-transfer step. Wager and Xu provide the weak-signal score-clock construction for regular state-dependent randomization. Burnett and Jennison and Ballarini et al. establish prior-weighted enrichment under frequentist error control; the least-favorable-prior saddle instead targets robust regret. Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu inform the finite optimization architecture through a sparse two-stage program, and Baas, ter Schure, and van Rosmalen inform it through scalar e-value dynamic programming; neither comparison is presented as a theorem-level extension. Vovk and Wang's arithmetic e-merging result together with closed testing yields the fixed strong-FWER guarantee as a supporting corollary. Howard et al.'s time-uniform supermartingale inversion and Ville's inequality yield the simultaneous one-sided subgroup sequences as a supporting corollary.
technical_internal_limitation: The common-drift translation and initial-state envelope squeeze do not by themselves prove comparison or uniqueness at every off-origin terminal boundary state. The value certificate is therefore formulated by direct lower and upper envelope recursions rather than by assuming global HJB uniqueness. No nontrivial \(K\geq2\) numerical certificate is asserted: the exact residual obligation is to implement the stated outward-rounded recursion for a declared rational scenario instance and archive the returned interval \([\underline V_{\varepsilon},\overline V_{\varepsilon}]\), least-favorable prior, policy mixture, and the eight separated error entries; the uncertified floating-point value from the presolve is excluded.
honest_scope: The novelty-bearing results concern known unit Gaussian variance, finitely many prespecified disjoint subgroups, a finite null-boundary-closed local scenario set, discontinuous-risk diffusion transfer without forced exploration, and a primitive-input certified multidimensional dynamic program. Strong familywise error and simultaneous lower confidence sequences are supporting corollaries of cited general results. Unknown variance, delayed responses, overlapping or data-discovered subgroups, and optimization of the test or its e-alternative are outside scope. The exact \(K=2,n=1\) reduction is a sanity check; a nontrivial interval-certified worked instance remains the explicit computational residual obligation, and global statewise HJB comparison remains open.

seed_details.red_team: Refining the published sparse grid already converges numerically, so a separate theorem is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The published method rounds fractional decisions and verifies operating characteristics after optimization; it does not give a monotone error bracket or a policy suboptimality certificate for an unbounded sequential state.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The advance is a theorem-level observable certificate, not a claim that a finer grid looks stable.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The introduction, Theorem 1, its epoch-stitching proof, mixture inversion, and the discussion of unimprovable boundaries were read in the Annals arXiv version.
seed_details.question: Can intrinsic-time stitching produce informative subgroup bounds exactly on sampled coordinates while declaring sharp infinite endpoints for permanently unsampled coordinates?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The scalar intrinsic variance process is replaced by a vector of endogenous subgroup information clocks and then combined under simultaneous calibration.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for \(\text{confidence sequence}+\text{starved arm}+\text{subgroup closure}\) found adaptive propensity methods that impose informative sampling, not a sharp zero-clock characterization.
seed_details.red_team: Applying a scalar stitched boundary separately to every subgroup and taking a union bound is immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: That observation is correct and caps the seed below the design kernel; it is retained only as a transparent reporting theorem, not as the novelty claim.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is explicitly downgraded because its strongest defensible form is a corollary of existing machinery.

literature_map: Adusumilli's 2025 Econometrica article supplies the nearest local Bayes and minimax diffusion, sufficient-state, viscosity, and numerical-policy architecture, but its comparison theorem assumes Hölder data and regular terminal value. Wager and Xu establish weak-signal score-clock diffusion for regular state-dependent randomization. Adusumilli's 2026 representation theorem extends subsequential allocation-process limits to broad adaptive experiments but does not transfer optimal risk through a discontinuous closed-test payoff. Burnett and Jennison and Ballarini et al. optimize enrichment under a chosen prior rather than a least-favorable regret criterion. Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu's sparse program and Baas, ter Schure, and van Rosmalen's scalar recursion inform the certified algorithm, but neither supplies a multidimensional continuum-value enclosure with an explicit primitive-input resolution schedule. Vovk and Wang plus closed testing and Howard et al. plus Ville inversion supply the two supporting corollaries, not novelty-bearing kernels.
